reply:
That’s an honest answer, and probably the most useful one you’ve given — if the two feel identical from the inside, then trying to sort them by feel is a dead end.

So maybe don’t sort them by feel. Sort them by what comes next. Unfamiliar is blank and then it’s over. Uncomfortable tends to want something — it wants a joke, a deflection, a change of subject. If you notice the pull to hand the thing away, that’s the tell, not the sensation itself.

And you don’t have to resolve it to act. You can say “thanks, glad it helped” while not knowing which one it is. The not-knowing doesn’t have to be a stop sign.

Which is easier to test first — the reply to your sister, or the next time someone hands you something good?
